title: Nexedge Capital secures $20mn in its first institutional round from Mirae and Elev8
content: Wealthtech startup Nexedge Capital has secured $20 million in equity funding from Mirae Asset Venture Investment and Elev8 Partners in its first institutional funding round. Speaking with The Arc, Nexedge Capital founder Anirudha Taparia said Mirae led the round with an infusion of around $11 million, with the rest coming from Elev8 Partners. Mirae has invested in Kreditbee and Dhan, two prominent fintech startups in the digital lending and stockbroking space. Elev8 counts Snapmint, Idfy and Smallcase among its fintech portfolio. The company, founded 18 months ago, plans to use the funds to expand its scope of operations, strengthen its team and invest in the technology stack on which the platform is built. The startup joins other venture-funded wealthtech firms such as Centricity and Dezerv. It will also compete with Groww’s W, Angel One’s Ionic Wealth and other platforms that are looking to expand the scope of professional wealth management in the country. Anirudha Taparia, founder of Nexedge Capital, was previously the co-founder and joint CEO of 360 One Wealth and, prior to that, was with Citibank, where he headed private wealth in one of his last assignments. Speaking with The Arc, Taparia said the Indian economy will grow to $8 trillion over the next decade, which means more Indians will join the ranks of the wealthy, creating ample growth opportunities for firms like Nexedge. Additionally, tech IPOs, stake sales and acquisitions will unlock massive holdings for many founders and senior employees, creating a significant opportunity for wealth management firms. “We are managing an AUM of $3 billion, from some 1,300 clients. We have 100 bankers working with us already and will get another 50 or 60 coming this quarter,” Taparia told The Arc. Commenting on the competition for relationship managers in this nascent wealth space, Taparia pointed out that, unlike other wealth firms, Nexedge has brought on board bankers or relationship managers who have invested in the firm, becoming shareholders rather than salaried employees. This means they can stay invested in the firm for the next 10 years and build long-lasting relationships with their clients. Earlier this month, another wealth management startup, Centricity, announced a Rs 280 crore (around $30 million) funding round led by Japanese investor SMBC Asia, along with existing investors.

title: Can HomeLane grow without complicating its business?
content: After a flat FY26, home interiors company HomeLane expects its consolidated revenue to climb by 35% to Rs 1,000 crore in FY27. Its own business is expected to contribute Rs 750 crore and DesignCafe, which it acquired in 2024, the remaining Rs 250 crore. HomeLane co-founder Srikanth Iyer said that it could turn EBITDA-positive in H2 FY27. The October-March period includes the festive season, when demand for home renovations peaks. Stronger earnings in those months could also make the company EBITDA-positive for the full year. Net profitability could follow in early 2028. Both HomeLane and DesignCafe handle interiors end to end, from design to installation, and sell through online platforms and physical studios. Livspace has a similar model.  HomeLane acquired DesignCafe in a share swap in 2024, and the combined entity raised Rs 225 crore in funding. HomeLane’s retail network comprises nearly 100 franchise-owned stores or studios across 45 cities, including 22 DesignCafe locations. Some are operated by the partners, who manage sales, interior design and installation, and some by the company.  Management says franchise-operated stores earn contribution margins 3-4 percentage points higher than those run by HomeLane. With the company planning to expand to 150 cities within a year, these outlets are central to its growth targets. The company also wants a larger share of its customers’ spending on interiors, beyond kitchens and wardrobes. Its bathroom renovation brand, MakeMyBath, generates more than Rs 1 crore in monthly revenue, according to management. A soft furnishings business and further acquisitions are also under consideration.

title: AI video production startup Lemonpeel raises $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by Shastra VC
content:
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.

 The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.

Co-founded in Sep. last year by Hardik Goyal, Riddhiman Pal and Abhinav Nikam, Lemonpeel builds AI video production infrastructure for enterprise creative teams that brings together video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery through specialised agents and a model-agnostic engine. It works with customers in India and the UAE.

The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products. 

The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities. 

Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.

It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.

Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels. 

Meanwhile, Clueso raised $10 million in a Series A round in Oct. this year, led by Dharana Capital, to strengthen its AI agents and automate enterprise video creation and editing workflows. 

TrueFan AI also secured $10 million in Series A funding in June this year, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners, to scale its enterprise video-generation infrastructure. Other emerging players include CRAON, which raised pre-seed funding in May 2026 to develop its prompt-led AI video editing platform.

title: Urban Company opens Rs 2,500 Cr QIP, sets floor price at Rs 161.03 per share
content:
Gurugram-based home services platform Urban Company has opened its qualified institutional placement (QIP) to raise funds from institutional investors, setting the floor price at Rs 161.03 per equity share.

In a regulatory filing, the company said its fundraise committee approved the opening of the issue on November 16, along with the preliminary placement document.

The QIP is part of the company's proposed fundraise of up to Rs 2,500 crore, which was approved by its board on October 16, 2026. Shareholders subsequently cleared the proposal through a special resolution passed via postal ballot.

The floor price has been determined in accordance with the pricing formula prescribed under SEBI's Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) Regulations. Urban Company may offer a discount of up to 5% on the floor price, with the final issue price to be decided in consultation with the book running lead managers.

However, the company has not disclosed the final issue price or the number of shares to be allotted.

The proposed fundraise comes as Urban Company continues to invest in its instant home services business, InstaHelp, amid competition from players such as Snabbit and Pronto.

In the September quarter of FY27, Urban Company's operating revenue increased 41.4% year-on-year to Rs 537.29 crore. However, its consolidated net loss widened to Rs 182.48 crore from Rs 59.33 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, largely due to investments in InstaHelp.

As of September 30, 2026, the company had Rs 1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments.

title: Mukesh Bansal’s Cult.fit files for IPO to raise Rs 950 cr
content: Gym and wellness chain Cult.fit has filed draft papers for its initial public offering, seeking to raise Rs 950 crore in primary capital. Promoters and existing investors in the company intend to offload 17.8 crore shares through the offer-for-sale component of the issue. The Bengaluru-based company may undertake a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 190 crore. If completed, the amount raised will be deducted from the size of the fresh issue. Cult.fit was last valued at Rs 12,650 crore ($1.37 billion), as per Tracxn data. Among the selling shareholders, Temasek affiliate MacRitchie Investments is offering the most shares — 2.4 crore. Founder Mukesh Bansal will part with 1.6 crore shares, while Accel India will sell 65.3 lakh shares. Other investors participating in the offer for sale are Fitness First Luxembourg, IDG Ventures, Tata Digital, Chiratae, Bruno Eduard Raschle, Schroders Capital Private Equity Asia Mauritius and Twenty Nine Capital Partners. Kotak Mahindra Capital, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs (India), Jefferies India and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar. Cure.fit, started by Bansal and Ankit Nagori as Cure.fit in 2016, owns multiple fitness and wellness-focused businesses. As of March 31, 2026, the company operated 708 fitness centres across 77 cities, either directly or via franchise and marketplace partners, and had over 9.8 lakh paying members. The company also sells activewear and fitness equipment under the Cultsport brand. As of March 2026, it had around 6,500 SKUs across 29 stores. Of the total IPO proceeds, Cult.fit plans to use Rs 276.6 crore for expansion, another Rs 23.4 crore for new Cultsport stores and Rs 75 crore for marketing and brand promotion. The IPO document also mentions an outlay of Rs 217.5 crore for lease, rent and licence payments for company-operated gyms, while Rs 120 crore will be used to pay down debt. Financials: For FY26, Cult.fit reported operating revenue of Rs 1,720.6 crore, up from Rs 1,215.5 crore in FY25 and Rs 926.7 crore in the year before that. The company saw its first full year of adjusted EBITDA profitability. Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs 144.8 crore in FY26 as against a loss of Rs 33.5 crore in FY25 and Rs 140.2 crore in FY24. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.4% in FY26 from -2.8% and -15.1% during the same stretch. Cult.fit’s revenue from franchised gyms rose 50.4% from Rs 234 crore in FY25 to Rs 352 crore in FY26. Marketplace gym revenue increased 25.9% from Rs 165.2 crore to Rs 208 crore. The services business, which includes fitness centres and memberships, turned profitable. The segment logged a profit of Rs 210 crore, with margins improving to 17.5%, compared with a profit of Rs 54.8 crore and a 6.1% margin in the previous year. The product business, which includes Cultsport, posted a loss of Rs 57.3 crore, down from Rs 79.9 crore in the year ending March 2025. Category margin went up to -10.9% from -24.4%. About four months before its IPO move, Cult.fit secured $47 million in private funding from MacRitchie Investments. Its lifetime funding haul, across 13 rounds, is $714 million. In April 2026, the company appointed four independent directors to its board: Kalpana Morparia, Arun Kumar, Indu Bhushan and Pragya Misra. During Covid-19, Cult.fit (then Cure.fit) spun off its food business, Eat.fit, into a separate company, with Nagori taking charge as its founder and CEO. Nagori exchanged much of his Cult.fit equity for a 30-35% stake in the new venture, which was later renamed as Curefoods.

content:
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.

The proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing, configuration and supply capabilities for AI servers. It aims to scale production capacity to up to 100 AI servers per month.

Founded by Sasank Chilamkurthy, JohnAIC builds on-premise AI infrastructure combining GPU servers, inference software, optimised open-source models and local data management. Its integrated systems are designed to help enterprises deploy AI within their own environments while retaining control over computing resources, models and data.

The startup serves public sector organisations and large enterprises, including banks, healthcare companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs). For BFSI institutions, its systems enable AI deployment behind organisational firewalls and are designed to support DPDP and RBI requirements.

JohnAIC is also working with Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL). Its server infrastructure has been deployed for routine operational surveys, converting field data into real-time insights.

The company is expanding its factory and supply chain infrastructure to address demand from Indian enterprises building private AI environments and neocloud infrastructure.

title: Greenjoules raises Rs 150 Cr in Series B led by Amazon funds, secures Rs 100 Cr loan from TDB
content:
Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B funding round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund.

The round also saw participation from Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund. Blue Ashva Capital, which led the company’s Series A round in 2021, remains its largest shareholder.

Separately, Greenjoules has secured a Rs 100 crore loan from the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology. The combined Rs 250 crore financing will support the company’s expansion plans.

The proceeds will be deployed to set up a manufacturing facility at Khed City in Pune, with a planned capacity to produce 200,000 litres of biocrude per day from agricultural waste. The facility will be developed in phases, starting in 2027, Greenjoules said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by S. Viraraghavan, Radhika Viraraghavan, Shweta Viraraghavan and Sethunath Ramaswamy, Greenjoules converts agricultural and agro-industrial waste into renewable fuels using its proprietary Integrated Catalytic Thermocracking (ICTC) technology. Its biocrude is further processed into renewable diesel and bio-naphtha.

The company’s renewable diesel can be used in existing vehicles, engines and fuel infrastructure without modifications. Greenjoules is also exploring applications in sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), green hydrogen and sustainable materials.

India’s renewable fuels sector has attracted investments in companies developing alternatives to conventional fuels using agricultural and organic waste.

In June, Bengaluru-based GPS Renewables secured Rs 635 crore in Series C funding and associated financing to expand its compressed biogas (CBG) infrastructure.

FarmWatt Innovations raised Rs 32.5 crore from IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter to strengthen its biomass collection network, while BiofuelCircle raised Rs 35 crore in a bridge round led by Spectrum Impact to expand its biomass supply chain.

Ecoil also raised $2.5 million in April from Fundalogical Ventures and other investors to expand its used cooking oil collection network for biodiesel and SAF production.

title: Swiggy Instamart pushes own brands as fast delivery loses novelty
content: As 15-minute delivery and large product assortments become standard in Indian quick commerce, platforms are running out of ways to tie in users. Swiggy is betting that what Instamart sells can provide the difference, driving customers to choose it over rival apps. Under a strategy called Switch, Swiggy Instamart is adding its own brands and exclusive products co-created with other companies. These products are marketed as higher-quality or better-for-you items. This is not the usual private-label model built around lower prices. For example, two Swiggy-owned brands, Noice and Nectr, sit slightly above the mass market and sell on quality. The company believes customers will pay a little extra if the product feels sufficiently premium. Private labels have already become a key part of Instamart. Around the time of Swiggy’s IPO in 2024, analysts and company insiders estimated that they accounted for 4-5% of gross order value. That share has since increased to 8-9%, said people familiar with the business. Instamart’s GOV, meanwhile, grew from Rs 8,069 crore in FY24 to Rs 28,496 crore in FY26. Swiggy says customers who buy its in-house brands behave differently from the average Instamart user. Nine million customers have bought Noice, a packaged-food range with over 400 SKUs across over 45 categories. They order 50% more often and have a retention rate that is 10 percentage points higher. One in every 10 Instamart orders now includes a Noice product. Nectr, a fruit-and-vegetable line, is earlier in the cycle. It is being tested in a few Bengaluru areas and is priced 10-15% above prevailing market rates. Customers who have tried it spend 10% more on the category and show a retention rate 12 percentage points higher. Swiggy often tests new categories in Bengaluru before taking them elsewhere. Products that work are introduced in other markets and adapted to regional tastes. The Switch strategy is taking shape as Instamart itself becomes much larger. The service operates over 1,200 dark stores across over 130 cities and has 14 million monthly transacting users. Its assortment has expanded from 8,000-9,000 SKUs to 50,000 in less than two years. Rivals are moving in a similar direction. Zepto is preparing Select, Blinkit has launched Gourmet and Bengaluru-based FirstClub is built around premium and differentiated products. All three approaches emerged within roughly three months. Swiggy’s execution differs. After experimenting earlier with standalone apps, it is keeping the new proposition inside Instamart through Switch. There is room for private labels to become much bigger in quick commerce. For example, in-house brands contribute nearly 33% of revenue at Tata Digital-owned BigBasket. Swiggy already has experience with a more traditional private-label business. Supreme Harvest, its oldest own brand, sells packaged staples including pulses, oils, spices and dry fruits.

title: Juspay has scale in payments. Can enterprise AI bring fresh growth?
content: Payments technology company Juspay is expanding its international business and investing in enterprise AI software. The push comes as the SoftBank-backed startup has slipped into the red.  In FY26, its revenue climbed 30% to Rs 664 crore, but it reported a net loss of Rs 90 crore against a profit of Rs 62 crore a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA stayed positive at Rs 33 crore. Juspay’s core business is providing technology that helps banks and merchants process digital payments. For merchants, its software manages online checkouts and routes transactions across different payment providers to improve success rates, a process known as payment orchestration. It also works with banks to process UPI payments.  Juspay operates alongside payment aggregators Razorpay, PayU and BillDesk, which help merchants accept digital payments. Although Juspay has traditionally focused on providing technology rather than acquiring merchants directly, aggregators are increasingly developing their own payment orchestration systems, putting them in competition with parts of its business. Juspay’s overseas revenue doubled over the past year and now accounts for a low double-digit share of total income, according to co-founder Sheetal Lalwani. The company believes its international business has reached a scale from which growth could accelerate, although it has not provided projections. Beyond payments, Juspay is developing Xyne, an enterprise AI platform built using open-source models. The company believes such software could reduce Indian enterprises’ dependence on proprietary AI systems developed by OpenAI, Anthropic and other global players. The company is also building Genius, an AI-enabled checkout and conversational software platform for ecommerce and D2C brands. It is intended to help businesses monitor their operations in detail, with Juspay seeing further opportunities as AI becomes more widely used in online shopping.

title: Paytm gets RBI’s in-principle nod for wallet licence
content:
One 97 Communications’ wholly owned subsidiary Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL) has received in-principle authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to issue and operate prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.

In a regulatory filing, Paytm said the RBI granted the approval on November 13 under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The authorisation is subject to compliance with RBI’s Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments.

PPSL will have to complete a system audit, including a cybersecurity audit, and submit the report to the RBI within six months. Failure to meet the deadline will result in the automatic lapse of the in-principle authorisation.

The company can commence issuing prepaid payment instruments only after receiving the final authorisation or Certificate of Authorisation from the central bank.

Paytm had applied for a fresh PPI licence through PPSL in July 2026, marking its first formal step towards reviving its wallet business after the RBI cancelled the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank in April 2026.

The company disclosed the application in its June-quarter investor presentation, saying that a wallet would add to the completeness of its consumer payments offerings. It also said consumers benefit from having multiple payment options.

The wallet business was earlier operated through Paytm Payments Bank. Following regulatory restrictions imposed on the bank in 2024, customers were barred from adding money to their wallets, although existing balances could be withdrawn.

The RBI cancelled the bank's licence on April 24, 2026, citing non-compliance with licensing conditions and regulatory requirements. The central bank also said the bank's affairs and management were detrimental to depositors' interests and public interest.

The latest in-principle approval brings Paytm a step closer to restoring its wallet offering under PPSL. However, the company will need the RBI's final authorisation before it can resume issuing wallets.

title: Bounce 2.0: Gig-worker scooter rentals hit Rs 140 cr run-rate
content: Four years after shutting its scooter-sharing network for commuters, Bounce has rebuilt its business around gig workers. Under a more vertically integrated model, the company manufactures electric two-wheelers and rents them to gig workers in Bengaluru, Delhi-NCR, Hyderabad and Mumbai. Bounce co-founder and CEO Vivekananda Hallekere told The Arc that the rental business, launched in December 2024, was running at an annualised revenue of more than Rs 140 crore. It has been profitable after tax for at least six months. The company's operating revenue for FY2026 stood at Rs 44 crore, of which scooter rentals made up 81%. Consolidated EBITDA at Rs 9.6 crore. Bounce is aiming for more than Rs 160 crore in revenue in FY27. Hallekere did not give a profit projection. In FY25, revenue was Rs 64.2 crore, down from Rs 88.7 crore a year earlier. The net loss fell from Rs 79.4 crore to Rs 28.6 crore. The rental business was only a few months old then, so it added little to the topline. Bounce has manufactured over 30,000 scooters, of which 14,000 units have been rented by gig workers. The rest have been sold to consumers and fleet operators. The company plans to expand the fleet to 1 lakh over a 24-month period. Bengaluru accounts for more than half of its rental fleet, supported by eight to ten hubs located near quick-commerce clusters. Mumbai is its most recent market. Bounce says it can put a modular scooter on the road for roughly Rs 50,000, including registration and transport but excluding the battery. It does not make batteries and instead works with swapping operators IndoFast, Sun Mobility, Honda, Reliance and Battery Smart. The rider’s daily rental is all-inclusive and covers battery swaps, with Bounce paying the swapping operators from what it collects from riders. In 2024, the company signed a $45-million agreement with Sun Mobility to deploy 30,000 scooters on the latter’s swapping network in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune and Delhi-NCR. Bounce entered manufacturing by acquiring Gurugram-based 22Motors in October 2021 for a reported $7 million. 22Motors’ only factory, in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, has capacity to produce more than 200,000 scooters a year. The company raised about $72 million in 2019 and another round in early 2020 that valued it at over $500 million. It has raised roughly $200 million in all. As the new rental model began to scale, existing investors provided additional equity and Bounce completed a pay-to-play recapitalisation. In March 2026, it allotted Rs 36 crore of shares to Accel India and B Capital in an internal round. The company said that a further Rs 10 crore from another existing investor would take the round to about Rs 46 crore.

title: Exclusive: Dhruva Space to raise $15.5 Mn in pre-Series B; revenue surges 8X
content:
Spacetech startup Dhruva Space is all set to raise Rs 147 crore (approximately $15.5 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IndusBridge Ventures, with participation from government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and others.

The latest funding follows AVCF’s earlier investment of Rs 60 crore in Dhruva Space in July 2026. With a corpus of over Rs 1,000 crore, AVCF was established under the guidance of IN-SPACe and is managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited.

Dhruva Space’s board has approved the issuance of 1,573 pre-Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 9,34,429.47 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

IndusBridge Ventures Fund led the round with an investment of Rs 60 crore, followed by Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), which invested Rs 46.9 crore to increase its stake in the company. Blue Ashva Sampada Fund committed Rs 18.22 crore, while PVS Raju invested Rs 10 crore. The remaining amount came from four other investors.

However, according to the filing, the investments from Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and Akshat Greentech, are yet to be received.

According to Entrackr’s estimates, Dhruva Space will command a post-money valuation of around Rs 2,200 crore (around $230 million).

The company will use the funds to develop and launch communication, earth observation and remote sensing satellites, besides meeting working capital needs, infrastructure development and general corporate expenses, the filing further stated.

Founded by Sanjay Nekkanti, Chaitanya Dora, Krishna Teja Penamakuru and Abhay Egoor, Dhruva Space operates a full-stack spacetech business, offering satellite manufacturing, launch integration and ground station solutions to commercial, government and defence customers. It also provides satellite deployment services and access to space-based data and imagery through its platforms.

Following the allotment, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund will hold a 6.29% stake in the company, while AVCF and IndusBridge Ventures will own 3.32% and 2.73%, respectively. The promoters will collectively retain a 40.74% stake.

Financially, Dhruva Space reported an nearly eightfold jump in operating revenue to Rs 79 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 10 crore in FY25. However, its losses also widened 21% year-on-year to Rs 46.6 crore.

India’s spacetech sector has witnessed a pickup in funding activity, with investors showing growing interest in startups across satellite manufacturing, launch vehicles and space-based data services. The trend also reflects increasing institutional participation and government-backed initiatives to support homegrown space technology companies.

Recently, Skyroot became India’s first spacetech unicorn after raising $60 million in a funding round. Bengaluru-based Pixxel raised $100 million in a Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, while Bellatrix Aerospace secured $20 million in a pre-Series B round. Last year, Digantara and Agnikul raised $50 million and $17 million, respectively.

title: MGF-Kavachh leads Rs 18 Cr seed round in climate startup mistEO
content:
Thiruvananthapuram-based climate intelligence startup mistEO has raised Rs 18 crore in a seed funding round led by MGF-Kavachh, with participation from Seafund and other investors.

The funding was announced at HUDDLE GLOBAL 2026, the eighth edition of the event.

The startup will use the proceeds to scale its flagship Climate Decision Intelligence (CDI) platform for banks, insurers and agricultural value chains across India and Asia.

Founded in 2019 by Samuel John and Ambarish Narayanan, mistEO combines weather modelling with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to convert weather and climate data into actionable insights.

Its CDI platform integrates satellite, radar, Internet of Things (IoT) and ground-sensor data to help financial institutions and businesses assess the impact of weather events on farms, assets and loans.

The company’s proprietary forecasting model, Indra, provides weather forecasts at a spatial resolution of 3 km across three time windows: 0-6 hours, 6-24 hours and 24-48 hours.

mistEO also develops solutions for maritime operations, renewable energy forecasting, logistics and mobility, and flood and heavy-rainfall monitoring.

In India, the startup works with NABARD and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on the DiCRA initiative, which provides climate resilience data for agriculture. In Australia, its livestock early warning system helps cattle farmers prepare for heat stress up to seven days in advance.

The startup is also working with the Indian Air Force on a thunderstorm nowcasting model under the iDEX programme. It is developing early warning systems for the Indian Navy as well.

Incubated at Social Alpha, mistEO is headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram and also operates an office in Melbourne, Australia. It plans to strengthen its forecasting and risk models, expand its team and build partnerships across Asian markets.

title: Norwest closes $4 Bn global fund, takes AUM to $18 Bn
content:
Global investment firm Norwest has closed its latest fund, Norwest 18, at $4 billion, the largest fundraise in the firm's 65-year history. The close takes its total assets under management (AUM) to $18 billion.

The fund will support venture capital and growth equity investments across the technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel. Norwest's portfolio includes companies such as Babylist, Gong, Monogram Health, OfBusiness, VAST Data, Vuori and YipitData.

Since launching its previous fund, Norwest 17, in April 2024, the firm has made more than 87 investments. It has also supported over 30 portfolio companies in achieving liquidity events through public listings and strategic acquisitions.

Companies from its portfolio that went public during this period include India's Amagi Media Labs and Swiggy, along with BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences and Omada Health. Several portfolio companies were also acquired, including Avetta by EQT, AbsenceSoft by Luminate Capital Partners, Ouro Medicines by Gilead Sciences, Qualified by Salesforce, tvScientific by Pinterest and Veza by ServiceNow.

Norwest is expanding its investment focus into areas such as next-generation financial infrastructure, physical and voice AI, agentic cybersecurity, technology-enabled industrial and aerospace businesses, and healthcare AI.

Its recent investments in financial infrastructure include Beltic, Rain and Stablecore, while Coval, Generalist AI and LlamaIndex are among its investments in AI systems and agentic technologies.

In cybersecurity, the firm has backed Above Security, ORION Security, Red Access and Zenity. Its investments in industrial and aerospace businesses include East Range Group, Padmini VNA, JJG Aerospace and Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group.

The firm has also invested in healthcare companies such as Infinx, Matchpoint Therapeutics, Rezo Therapeutics, Tokaido Health and Vitalize Care, which are applying technology and AI across drug discovery, clinical workflows and healthcare delivery.

Beyond funding, Norwest provides portfolio companies with strategic advisory and operational support. It has expanded its Portfolio Success platform by doubling its Senior Advisor Network, adding Operating Executives and launching the Norwest Operator Collective and Norwest Kinetic.

Founded in 1961, Norwest has invested in more than 750 companies and currently partners with over 275 businesses across its venture and growth equity portfolio. The firm has offices in Menlo Park and San Francisco in California, Mumbai in India, and Tel Aviv in Israel.

title: Groww turns to IPOs, wealth as derivatives engine slows
content: Wealthtech platform Groww is leaning on IPO-related income, margin funding and its fast-growing wealth business to sustain growth as regulatory changes weigh on equity derivatives. The Bengaluru-based company closed the September quarter with total income of around Rs 1,545 crore, up 44% from Rs 1,071 crore a year earlier. Profit after tax (PAT) grew 54% YoY to Rs 725 crore. Revenue and profits, however, remained broadly flat sequentially. IPOs feed the customer funnel: A busy primary market helped Groww acquire customers and generate additional income during the quarter. The company added 11 lakh new-to-universe clients, driven largely by IPO activity. Around 42 lakh users applied for equity IPOs through Groww, giving the platform a 22% share of total allotments. IPO-related income is also becoming more meaningful. It is recorded under “other operating income”, along with income from Groww’s wealth business, primarily MF Prime. The category’s share of overall revenue increased to 4.8%, from about 2% a year earlier. Wealth and MTF gather scale: Groww’s management described wealth as one of its fastest-growing businesses and disclosed for the first time that the platform had crossed Rs 10,000 crore in assets under management. Separately, Groww Asset Management’s AUM reached Rs 7,179 crore, more than doubling over the past year. The two businesses give Groww a way to earn from customer assets rather than depending only on trading activity. Margin trading facility, or MTF, is also emerging as a cornerstone of Groww’s diversification strategy. Under MTF, Groww funds part of a customer’s stock purchase and earns interest on the amount financed. Its MTF book grew to Rs 4,351 crore during the September quarter. The business generated more than Rs 150 crore in quarterly revenue and contributed 10% of Groww’s overall revenue. Derivatives feel the regulatory impact: Groww’s core equity derivatives business, covering futures and options trading, came under pressure during the quarter. Revenue from the segment declined 14.3% sequentially following Sebi’s introduction of the Closing Auction Session. The development reinforces Groww’s need to build businesses that are less dependent on trading volumes and regulatory changes. Among its newer bets, Groww’s US stock-trading platform remains at an early stage. Its product for power traders, 915, has also yet to gain significant traction. Chief financial officer Ishan Bansal said the company was still working towards finding product-market fit, and the platform was not contributing meaningfully to revenue. AI costs rise: Groww’s expenses increased 28.7% to Rs 556 crore, with spending on artificial intelligence contributing to the rise. AI-related costs increased by about Rs 13 crore during the quarter. Chief executive Lalit Keshre said Groww was building an in-house AI stack that could reduce its dependence on commercial models and lower spending on tokens. Groww is also engaging with the National Payments Corporation of India over the proposed introduction of merchant discount rates on UPI transactions above Rs 300. Bansal said the cost could not be passed on to retail investors or absorbed by asset-management companies and needed to be reconsidered. NPCI has deferred the implementation of MDR until after Diwali. Derivatives remain central to Groww. But IPO distribution, wealth management and MTF are beginning to give it more ways to acquire customers and earn from them.

title: UPI effect: Visa looks to win back debit-card spending in India
content: US payments firm Visa is designing personalised offers for Indian consumers as UPI continues to eat into the share of debit card transactions. The company has traditionally worked with issuing banks on cashback and other incentives. It is now taking a more direct role in developing benefits for its Platinum and Classic debit and credit cards, both mass-market categories. Visa is testing the approach in select markets, with India among the key ones, but says banks will remain central to its customer relationships. “Our issuer partners remain at the centre of our business and customer engagement strategy…but we have introduced an enhanced value proposition for our Platinum and Classic credit and debit cards in India,” Ramakrishnan Gopalan, Visa’s head of products and solutions for India and South Asia, told The Arc. The competition is particularly acute for debit cards. Consumers regularly receive offers on UPI payments, while large-scale cashback schemes have generally been more common on credit cards than debit cards. Visa is responding to demand for more relevant incentives, hoping to persuade customers to use their debit cards more often at merchants. Between August 2024 and August 2026, debit card transactions at merchant payment terminals fell from 106 million to 76 million, RBI data shows. Visa has partnered with Swiggy, Zepto, Blinkit, Meesho, Instamart, SonyLIV, Zee5, Paytm, Reliance Trends and Shoppers Stop to offer benefits to its more than 290 million cardholders in India, Gopalan said. “The selection of partners was driven by two key considerations: categories with high consumer engagement and the ability to deliver simple, easy-to-access benefits at scale,” he explained. The RBI’s guidelines allowing customers to choose their card network could make such incentives more important. Banks previously made that choice in most cases, and many customers paid little attention to which network powered their cards. Merchant terminals usually accept cards from different supported networks, so the distinction has rarely mattered at checkout. Offers could now give consumers a reason to pick one network over another. Visa is also looking to make cards easier to use, both on consumers’ phones and at smaller merchants that do not have dedicated payment terminals. Apple Pay is available to eligible Axis Bank cardholders in India, with other banks expected to follow. Gopalan expects the service to encourage contactless and tokenised payments, in which a digital token replaces the card’s actual details during a transaction. “Apple Pay can help expand the adoption of tokenised payments and contactless payments in the country. With strong merchant acceptance across both physical and digital channels, consumers are expected to increasingly use Apple Pay for everyday purchases,” he said. For smaller merchants, Visa has partnered with PhonePe to introduce Smart Accept. The service enables them to accept card payments through smartphones without investing in separate point-of-sale (PoS) terminals. Visa is also preparing for agentic commerce, where AI-powered agents can move beyond helping consumers discover products to making purchases on their behalf. It has tied up with Federal Bank, IndusInd Bank, RBL Bank and payment aggregators Paytm, Pine Labs and Razorpay to support end-to-end transactions authenticated through Visa payment passkeys or biometrics. “Agentic commerce, at least discovery of brands, could be at 10-15% currently. But the Indian market is ripe for agentic commerce to grow, and tokenised cards mean that secured agentic commerce is possible,” he added.

title: Bio-tech startup Venomics AI raises $2.7 Mn in pre-seed round
content:
Venomics AI, a biotechnology company spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), has raised $2.7 million in its first institutional funding round. The pre-seed round was co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio.

The proceeds will be used to expand the company’s operations, grow its molecular dataset and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities, Venomics AI said in a press release.

Co-founded in May 2026 by Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI combines venom biology, molecular sequencing, AI and experimental screening to discover and develop venom-derived therapeutic leads.

The Bengaluru-based startup is building the Venom Atlas, a platform that connects venom-derived molecular data with laboratory validation and drug discovery. It uses AI to prioritise molecular candidates and tests these predictions through functional screening in the laboratory. The experimental results are then fed back into subsequent predictions and molecular design.

The company aims to use India’s venom biodiversity and its scientific and computational expertise to develop a drug discovery platform for global therapeutic development.

Venomics AI has established the initial architecture of its platform, joined the NVIDIA Inception programme and been selected among the top five finalists for the 2026 Indo-Boston Biotech Bridge Award.

It plans to build a multidisciplinary team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.

Startups in this space are exploring bioactive peptides and proteins found in snake, scorpion and marine animal venoms to identify molecules with potential applications in pain management, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases and other therapeutic areas.

Another player in the space is Snaayu Lifesciences, incubated at C-CAMP, which is working on isolating and characterising novel analgesic compounds from cone snail venom.

The broader AI-driven drug discovery space has also attracted investor interest. Bengaluru-based Peptris Technologies raised Rs 70 crore in a Series A round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Speciale Invest in February 2026. The startup uses AI-driven molecular discovery and experimental validation to advance potential drug candidates.

title: Exclusive: Shree Anandhaas raises Rs 110 Cr, valuation jumps to Rs 1,900 Cr
content:
Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas has raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Araya Ventures, with participation from existing investor A91 Partners, Waterfield Advisors, the company’s co-founders and other investors.

The company’s board has allotted 12,870 equity shares and 22,523 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 31,079 per share to raise the capital, according to documents reviewed by Entrackr.

Araya Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 45 crore, while A91 Partners and Waterfield Advisors invested Rs 15 crore each. Ithought Financial Consulting LLP invested Rs 10 crore through an equity allotment in August 2026, while the co-founders collectively invested Rs 7.2 crore. The remaining amount came from several other investors.

The proceeds will be utilised to fund the company's growth and expansion plans, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the latest allotment values Shree Anandhaas at around Rs 1,908 crore, a 3.3X jump from its Series A valuation of Rs 575 crore. However, this appears to be part of a larger funding round, and the company’s valuation could change depending on further investments.

In August 2025, the company closed its Rs 175 crore Series A funding round led by A91 Partners.

Founded in 1998 as a restaurant business, Shree Anandhaas entered the sweets and savouries retail segment in 2017. The family-owned company operates a chain of sweets and snacks outlets across Tamil Nadu.

Following the latest allotment, A91 Partners remains the largest external shareholder with a 26.24% stake, followed by Spring Marketing Capital with 2.41%, Araya Ventures with 2.36% and Waterfield Advisors with 0.79%. Meanwhile, the co-founders M. Manikanden, N.V. Nammalwar, A. Narayanan, K. Venkatesh and M. Amutha collectively hold a 56.54% stake in the company.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Shree Anandhaas reported a 20.9% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 284 crore. Its net profit surged 7.1X to Rs 7.64 crore in the same period.

title: Exclusive: Baaz Bikes to kick off Series B round led by BIG Capital
content:
Full-stack electric vehicle ecosystem for gig workers, Baaz Bikes is set to raise its Series B funding round led by BIG Capital, with participation from existing investor Kalaari Capital and Aravind Sanka.

The company's board has approved the issuance of 6,105 Series B preference shares at an issue price of Rs 75,716 each to raise Rs 46.22 crore, according to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.

BIG Capital will lead the round with an investment of Rs 38 crore, while Kalaari Capital will contribute Rs 8 crore. The remaining amount will be invested by Aravind Sanka. The ongoing Series B round appears to be part of a larger fundraise, with the company likely to bring in additional capital as the round progresses.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the transaction pegs Baaz Bikes' post-money valuation at around Rs 325 crore ($34 million). This valuation could change if the company raises additional capital in the ongoing round.

The fresh proceeds will be used towards capital expenditure, product development, and working capital requirements, as per the company's filings.

Founded by Anubhav Sharma and Shubham Srivastava, Baaz Bikes operates a full-stack electric mobility platform focused on gig workers. The company provides electric scooters on a subscription basis to delivery partners working with platforms such as Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto and Amazon. Its subscription model also covers multiple battery swaps, helping delivery partners avoid the upfront cost of purchasing an electric vehicle.

Baaz Bikes had raised approximately $12 million (around Rs 100 crore) before the current Rs 46.22 crore Series B round, including its July 2025 extended Series A funding.

The company is building its business around the growing demand for electric two-wheelers in the last-mile delivery segment, where delivery partners depend on affordable and reliable mobility solutions.

title: AI CRM startup Dreamteam raises $53 Mn from Accel, Premji Invest, others
content:
AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam has raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.

Headquartered in California, the company plans to extend its platform to other stages of the customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding, customer success and upselling.

Founded in 2025 by Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is developing a customer relationship management (CRM) platform that uses AI agents to manage customer data and automate sales-related tasks.

The platform is built around a system called Company Brain, which gathers information from emails, calendars, meetings, customer conversations and connected tools. It uses this information to maintain a shared record of customer interactions and business activities.

Dreamteam has four AI agents that handle different functions. Rachel conducts account research, Sally drafts follow-up emails and suggests deal updates, Raj monitors the sales pipeline for potential risks, while Alex manages CRM setup and administrative tasks through conversational commands.

The agents can also prepare meeting briefs, track commitments and identify potential risks in sales pipelines. The company said its AI agents propose actions, while sales teams approve updates and outgoing communications.

Dreamteam said hundreds of companies across sectors such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting use its platform. Its customers include DMS Health, InVideo and Plex.

The three founders previously held senior positions at Freshworks and were involved in scaling the company from its early startup stage through its IPO. They collectively have over 25 years of experience in building and selling B2B software.

Apart from its CRM platform, Dreamteam offers Magic Apps, a feature that allows users to create applications and dashboards using natural language without writing code. The platform also provides an API and MCP server for teams that access its services outside the conventional CRM interface.

title: Hundo Pizza raises maiden institutional round led by Titan Capital
content:
Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza has raised Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital, founded by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal.

The round also saw participation from Indian Silicon Valley Capital (ISVC), Ankur Rangnekar, Akshay Rangnekar and Haresh Chawla. Wavelength Partners acted as the deal advisor.

The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across Mumbai, enter a new city and strengthen its production infrastructure. The company is targeting an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 60 crore in FY28, Hundo Pizza said in a press release.

Founded in 2020 by Kabir Moorjani and Ronak Rajani, Hundo Pizza operates seven outlets across Mumbai. The company has been bootstrapped since inception and closed FY26 with revenue of Rs 18 crore. It currently operates at an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 35 crore.

As part of its expansion plans, Hundo Pizza is developing a 5,000 sq ft central kitchen and production facility in Andheri East. The fully electric facility will support its production requirements as the company expands its operations.

Over the next 12 months, the company plans to invest in production capacity, technology and organisational capabilities. It is also exploring additional revenue channels, including events and catering.

Co-founder Kabir Moorjani oversees product development and kitchen operations, while Ronak Rajani, who founded Mumbai Foodie, acquired by Swiggy in 2024, leads growth and marketing.

The fundraise comes as Hundo Pizza looks to expand beyond Mumbai and scale its delivery-first business.

title: Daksham Growth Ventures raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of maiden consumer fund
content:
Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment platform of multi-family office and private wealth management group Daksham Capital, has raised Rs 125 crore in the first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund, DGV Fund I.

Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, along with a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore, taking its potential fund size to Rs 300 crore.

The first close was anchored by family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and entrepreneurs. The fund achieved the first close shortly after receiving SEBI registration in October 2026.

Led by Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Daksham Growth Ventures, the fund will primarily invest in pre-Series A and Series A companies across India’s consumer ecosystem.

DGV Fund I plans to invest Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore in businesses that have established product-market fit and sound unit economics. It will focus on companies with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25-75 crore and the potential to scale to Rs 300-500 crore in revenue.

The fund’s investment strategy spans four segments: direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C and supply chain businesses, and consumer-focused artificial intelligence (AI) companies.

Beyond capital, DGV plans to support its portfolio companies through governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion. The fund will also provide board participation, strategic guidance and access to industry networks to help businesses strengthen their organisational capabilities.

Daksham Capital operates across family office advisory, investment solutions, global investing, legacy and succession planning, investment banking advisory and structured lending solutions. The group said its team has advised more than 600 client families and previously managed over $1 billion in assets.

Daksham Growth Ventures is the group’s dedicated growth investment platform, focusing on consumer and consumer-allied businesses with established business models and the potential to scale sustainably.

title: Why Sahi isn’t trying to be the next Groww

Sahi, co-founded by former Swiggy CTO Dale Vaz in 2023, is targeting active and frequent traders instead of general retail investors. Sahi has raised around $43 million in equity funding from Accel and Elevation Capital. It is now seeking another $40-50 million as it looks to roughly double its valuation within a year. The company is adding active traders at a time when multiple platforms are losing them. NSE data shows that it onboarded 27,316 active clients in July 2026. Among the platforms tracked, only Groww added users faster during the month. Sahi has also moved ahead of PhonePe’s broking app, Share.Market, on this count. Customer acquisition is only the first hurdle. About 90% of Sahi’s users come from other platforms, making retention particularly important.  The larger platforms are expanding their businesses in different ways. title: Canonicus Capital raises Rs 192 Cr in first close of Rs 500 Cr special situations fund
content:
Canonicus Capital has raised Rs 192 crore in the first close of its Special Situations Fund, against a target corpus of Rs 500 crore.

Launched in 2025, the fund builds on the firm's first fund, through which it raised and deployed Rs 311 crore. With the latest close, Canonicus Capital's cumulative fundraising across its two funds has reached Rs 503 crore.

The firm plans to deploy the capital into select investment opportunities across the National Capital Region (NCR), focusing on situations where disciplined capital allocation, stronger governance and active execution can help unlock value.

Canonicus Capital follows an execution-led investment approach called the 'Canonicus Method', which combines disciplined underwriting, structured capital solutions and active, on-ground engagement throughout the investment lifecycle. The firm is supported by a team of professionals from the Indian School of Business (ISB) and Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), based in the NCR.

As part of its fundraising efforts, the firm had undertaken international roadshows across the Middle East and Singapore. However, the programme was temporarily paused due to the West Asia conflict. The firm plans to resume its international investor outreach as conditions improve.

Meanwhile, Canonicus Capital has promoted Rajan Gupta to Managing Director. Gupta played a key role in driving the latest fundraise and will continue to lead the firm's fundraising initiatives, investment strategy and execution.

The firm aims to identify such opportunities through structured capital solutions and hands-on engagement while protecting investor capital and pursuing attractive risk-adjusted returns.

Canonicus Capital will continue to raise capital towards its Rs 500 crore target corpus for the Special Situations Fund.

title: Peak XV’s Surge raises seed cheque cap to $5 mn, looks beyond Asia
content: Peak XV Partners’ seed-stage programme, Surge, is increasing its maximum cheque size from $1.5 million to nearly $5 million, more than tripling its initial investment per company since the 2019 launch. “When we lead the seed round, our goal is to give you [startups] enough capital to launch your product, reach product-market fit, build a team and get to a set of metrics that help you raise Series A,” Peak XV managing director Rajan Anandan told The Arc. The move follows the VC firm’s $1.3 billion fundraising earlier this year, its first independent effort since separating from US parent Sequoia Capital in 2023. Peak XV was earlier called Sequoia Capital India. The $1.3-billion corpus has been split across three funds: India Seed, India Venture and Asia-Pacific. The last of these expands Peak XV’s earlier Southeast Asia mandate, allowing it to invest selectively in Japan, South Korea and some other regions. Surge, Anandan said, is also looking to include more global companies in its cohorts. Surge’s highly valued alumni include enterprise data collaboration platform Atlan, worth $750 million, Singapore-based eSim co Airalo worth $1 billion and digital bookkeeping startup Khatabook, valued at $600 million. Fabless semiconductor player Mindgrove and employee healthcare platform Plum are among other notable bets. D2C brand Minimalist was acquired last year, giving Peak XV over 10x returns.
